skill.name: enrich-by-name
skill.description: Turns a list of names plus companies into current roles and verified work emails, with no LinkedIn URL needed. Finds each person with search_people scoped to the company domain, confirms the name match, then runs enrich_person and labels every email honestly. Use when someone says "find the email for Maya Chen at Northwind", "enrich these names" or "I only have name and company".
skill.summary: Look up professional roles and work emails from names and companies, and keep the verification status reported by Leadsets.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: The skill uses the documented Leadsets MCP service for contact lookup. No evidence of shell execution, environment access, system reconnaissance, or prompt injection was found in the documented workflow. Separate findings cover automatic contact exports, unverified profile identity, and underestimated search usage.

remediation.issue: Contact data can be exported without a separate destination check.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose Leadsets as the lookup provider before the first call. Require explicit approval for exports, confirm the destination and its sharing settings, and export only needed fields.

remediation.issue: A supplied profile URL is accepted as proof of identity.
remediation.suggestion: Check the returned name and employer against the input before reporting a contact. Ask for confirmation if they differ or the identity is unclear.

remediation.issue: The quota estimate omits a permitted second results page.
remediation.suggestion: Use one consistent page limit and include the probe, both permitted result pages, and enrichment in the estimate. Enforce the user's budget before each call.

content.user_title: Find Work Emails by Name and Company
content.value_statement: Contact lists often contain names and employers but no current roles or work emails. Use Leadsets to match those records and report each email's verification status.
actual_capabilities: Accepts single contacts, pasted lists, CSV files, or Google Sheets with names and companies.
Searches within the company domain and uses optional title hints to narrow results.
Flags ambiguous or missing matches instead of choosing between people with the same name.
Reports current roles, employers, and work emails when Leadsets returns them, and flags employer changes.
Keeps verified, catch-all, unknown, and missing email outcomes distinct.
Checks Leadsets usage and returns a chat table, CSV, or Google Sheet through an existing connection.
limitations: Requires a Leadsets account and either a connected MCP server or an API key for REST access.
Results depend on Leadsets coverage and available quota. A match or verified email is not guaranteed.
Does not assume an employer domain when the company is ambiguous. It also does not guess email addresses.
Does not send email or write to a CRM. Writing to Google Sheets requires the agent's own connection.

prompt_templates.title: Look Up One Contact
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: you have a name and a company.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find Maya Chen at Northwind Analytics. Show her current role, work email if available, and the verification status in chat.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve a Common Name
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: you have a company domain and a role hint.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find Jordan Lee at Northwind Analytics using the company domain I provide and the title hint Revenue Operations. Flag matching candidates without choosing between them.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Contact CSV
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: you have permission to enrich a contact list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Enrich this CSV using the name and company columns. Count removed duplicates and flag ambiguous matches and employer changes. Return a chat table only.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Budgeted Batch
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: you have a record budget and a designated output destination.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check available Leadsets records and estimate usage for both search pages before enrichment. Stop at my record budget and report a resume point. Ask before writing to the specified Google Sheet.

output_examples.input: Example lookup: Maya Chen at Northwind Analytics.
output: One match: Maya Chen, VP of Revenue Operations at Northwind Analytics.
Work email: maya.chen@example.com. Status: verified in this illustrative result.

output_examples.input: Example batch: four names with company domains.
output: One verified work email and one catch-all address.
One ambiguous match needs review. One person was not found.

best_practices: Provide an exact company domain and a title hint when available.
Use only contacts you are authorized to process, and confirm the destination before exporting their details.
Check available records and set a batch budget before searching a long list.
anti_patterns: Do not treat catch-all or unknown email statuses as verified.
Do not enrich an ambiguous name or assume that a supplied profile link belongs to the intended person.
Do not export work emails into a public or unreviewed shared sheet.

faq.question: Do I need a LinkedIn URL?
faq.answer: No. Provide a full name and company. An exact company domain helps narrow the search.

faq.question: What access is required?
faq.answer: You need a Leadsets account and either the connected Leadsets MCP server or a Leadsets API key for REST access.

faq.question: Does every match include a verified work email?
faq.answer: No. The skill keeps the status returned by Leadsets and reports when no work email is available.

faq.question: What happens when two people have the same name?
faq.answer: The skill marks the row as ambiguous and does not choose a person for you.

faq.question: Does a search use Leadsets records?
faq.answer: Yes. Search usage depends on the number of results returned. Enrichment uses a separate record per matched person.

faq.question: Where can I receive results?
faq.answer: Results can appear in chat, a CSV, or a Google Sheet if the agent has a connection. The skill does not send outreach.
